topic: Meyl scalar Faraday cage penetration — EXP-649 re-integration verification (ISS-2928)

holes_found.description: EXP-649's Q-factor resonant-enhancement patch (patch 2 of 2, targeting the '20 mV to 350 mV ... signals Meyl reports.' anchor) has been applied TWICE to data/wins.json WIN-015.detail_evidence, producing an exact 766-character duplicate block immediately adjacent to itself with zero gap between copies. The duplicated text runs verbatim from 'A defender might invoke resonant enhancement: Tesla-style bifilar coils tuned to their operating frequency...' through '...it does not carry the observation out of the reactive near-field regime into a domain where scalar waves would be required.' — appearing once at field offset 2368-3134 and again, byte-identical, at offset 3134-3900, before the field continues into the pre-existing 'The intervening Faraday cage does not rescue...' sentence. The find_pattern anchor ('20 mV to 350 mV ... signals Meyl reports.') itself occurs only once in the field, confirming the insertion point was correct both times — this is a re-application of the already-landed patch, not a wrong anchor. Root cause: this queue item's own `reason` field states 'Q-factor resonant-enhancement patch applied this run; Bruhn double-standard patch was already applied in a prior run' — but WIN-015.c6.json (cycle 6, reviewed 2026-07-12T05:45:00Z, queue_id=579) already confirmed BOTH EXP-649 patches landed cleanly with no duplication at that time. The Q-factor patch was therefore re-applied on/around 2026-07-17 despite already being present and previously verified, and the second application duplicated the appended sentences without duplicating the find_pattern prefix. This is a decider-side patch-reapplication bug (a target already satisfying an EXP's patch should be treated as landed and skipped, not reapplied) rather than an EXP-649 authoring defect — EXP-649's own patches are correct in isolation.
holes_found.recommendation: Delete the second verbatim copy: remove characters [3134, 3900) from WIN-015.detail_evidence in data/wins.json (766 chars, starting ' A defender might invoke resonant enhancement...' and ending '...where scalar waves would be required.'), restoring the field to exactly one copy of the Q-factor concession before 'The intervening Faraday cage does not rescue...' continues. Also recommend decider/tinker check whether the same re-application pattern hit any other EXP-649-adjacent target or any other recently-re-popped queue items around 2026-07-17, since the mechanism (re-running an EXP whose patches were already confirmed landed in a prior cycle's review) is generic and not specific to WIN-015.

seam_check: Check 2 (sed-seam artifacts): no double-period, double-comma, orphan punctuation, or unbalanced <em>/<sub>/<a> tags found anywhere in detail_evidence (0 occurrences of '..' or ',,' or ' ;'). The duplication itself is clean at the byte level (zero-gap, sentence-boundary-aligned, no broken markup) — it reads as a jarring repeated paragraph on a close read (Check 5) rather than a mangled seam, which is why it is flagged as a moderate content-duplication hole (Check 3 signal) rather than a Check-2 punctuation artifact.
adversarial_scan: Check 5: patch 1 (Bruhn double-standard) reads as a single coherent insertion — the internal-consistency-vs-empirical-claim distinction is clear, non-circular, and the anticipated 'isn't citing a preprint circular?' objection is preempted by the EXP's own anticipated_objections. No issues. Patch 2 (Q-factor) content is sound on a single read of ONE copy, but a careful reader hitting the duplicated block would immediately notice the identical paragraph repeating verbatim — this is the moderate hole above, not a new argumentative weakness. No double-negatives, units (mV/V, Q≈100, λ/2π) and citations (WPC Qi v1.3.1; Weinstein & Lafontaine IEEE 2009) remain correctly anchored to their claims in both copies.
summary_for_decider: EXP-649's two patches are both present in WIN-015.detail_evidence (Bruhn double-standard clean; Q-factor resonant-enhancement present but duplicated verbatim, 766 chars repeated back-to-back at offset 3134-3900). This is a re-application of a patch that c6 (2026-07-12) already confirmed had landed cleanly — a decider-side dedup/idempotency gap, not an EXP-649 authoring error. Recommend deleting the second copy (exact range given above) and checking whether other targets hit the same re-application pattern around this run. Verdict 'Not Demonstrated' is unaffected and holds.
